subject: Discovery recap: tool-calling & structured output (JSON schema)
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Cathy Liu <cathy.liu@acmeai.com>, Evan Ross <evan.ross@acmeai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: Discovery recap: tool-calling & structured output (JSON schema)

Hi Cathy / Evan —

Thanks again for a productive first call today. Quick recap below to make sure we captured pain, goals, and next steps around tool/function calling and structured output for your agent workflows. Please reply to confirm or correct anything I missed.

Pain points (what you told us):
- Current agents return freeform text; downstream systems need deterministic JSON for order creation and inventory updates (parsing failures cost ~5-10% of orders).
- Existing stack (Rasa + custom node microservices) struggles with high-latency LLM calls and unpredictable token costs.
- Hard to validate/monitor structured outputs in prod — lack of schema-level regression testing.

Current stack & constraints:
- Rasa for dialog state + internal microservices for fulfillment (Node.js).
- Hosting on GCP us-west, prefer not to send PII off-shore.
- Average user session size ~600 tokens; peak concurrent agent sessions ~40.

Success criteria (what success looks like):
1) Deterministic JSON output for key actions (create_order, update_inventory) conforming to a schema we can validate server-side.
2) End-to-end latency under 350ms p95 for single-turn agent calls in prod.
3) <1% schema-validation failures in first 90 days.
4) Clear observability for token usage per route + model variant fallback.

What we discussed re: technical approach
- Redwood can enforce a JSON schema and deterministic formatting via structured-output mode + example-driven prompts and strict schema verification.
- Suggest using a lightweight agent controller that calls Redwood's tool-calling API with an explicit JSON schema and post-call validators.
- Options for on-prem/private deployment if you need VPC-only traffic for PII-sensitive flows.

Proposed next steps
- I’ll share a proposed JSON schema for the two primary actions: create_order and update_inventory (attached).
- Schedule a 60-min tech deep-dive with your architect and our infra/engineer (Soojin) to review schema, performance targets, and deployment options.
- Draft a short mutual action plan (MAP) with milestones and decision points.

Availability: I have openings Mon/Tues next week 10-12 PT; if that doesn’t work share a few times and we’ll align.

Thanks — looking forward to mapping this out.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com | (415) 555-0192

Attachments: proposed-json-schema-v1.json (schema draft), redwood-product-one-pager.pdf

From: Cathy Liu <cathy.liu@acmeai.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>, Evan Ross <evan.ross@acmeai.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 15:38:12 -0800
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: tool-calling & structured output (JSON schema)

Thanks Jordan — this looks right to me. A few clarifications / additions:

- For create_order we need fields: order_id (string), customer_id (string), items [ {sku, qty, opt_modifiers} ], total_amount (decimal) and an optional notes field.
- Our inventory update must accept sku, warehouse_id, delta_qty (can be negative) and a timestamp in ISO8601.
- We absolutely need a strict failure mode: if the model returns anything that doesn't validate, we want a fast-fail (400) and a structured error payload.
- On latency: 350ms p95 is aggressive but reasonable if we use a dedicated model variant and tune batching.

I attached the sample schema you mentioned with a few comments inline — see proposed-json-schema-v1.json.

Also: Evan will own the SOC2/security checklist later in the procurement phase — he may request specific audit logs and evidence once we get to contract.

Cathy
Director of Product, Acme AI
Cathy.Liu@acmeai.com | +1 206 555 0110

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Cathy Liu <cathy.liu@acmeai.com>, Evan Ross <evan.ross@acmeai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 16:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: tool-calling & structured output (JSON schema)

Appreciate the clarifications, Cathy — this is super helpful. Quick follow-ups:

- I’ll incorporate your field set into the schema and add the strict failure-mode example (structured error payload).
- For validation flow: propose Redwood returns a validation status + error code; on failure your agent controller should return 400 with Redwood’s structured error payload (we’ll include example responses).
- For latency: Soojin (cc’d) can walk through dedicated model variant + batching knobs in the deep-dive.

Next concrete steps:
1) I’ll upload an updated schema and a one-pager on the validation/fast-fail contract by EOD Monday (attached to the MAP doc).
2) Marissa — can you pick 2 slots Mon/Tue 10-12 PT for the tech deep-dive?
3) Cathy / Evan — can you confirm who from infra will join?

Thanks — looping Marissa and Soojin to coordinate.

Best,
Jordan
